description: The trends in Maine are making it harder to start a family and have a baby. The state has lost twelve hospital-based birthing units, nine of them in just the past few years, including units at St. Mary's in Lewiston, Waldo Hospital in Belfast, and Houlton Regional Hospital. Rural Mainers whose closest hospital does not have a birthing unit now drive more than 45 minutes on average to reach the nearest hospital that delivers babies, the longest average drive time in New England. Distance from maternity care for families impacts both the safety and health outcomes for moms and babies.
